words.definition: A situation in which there are so many vehicles on the roads that traffic moves very slowly.
words.example: Traffic congestion in major cities costs the economy billions in lost working hours each year.

words.definition: A fee that drivers must pay to enter the busiest part of a city, intended to reduce traffic.
words.example: Since the introduction of a congestion charge, traffic levels in some city centres have fallen noticeably.

words.definition: The regular journey that someone makes between their home and their place of work.
words.example: A long daily commute can erode both productivity and the time people have for their families.

words.definition: Describing a transport system in which different types of transport are connected and work together efficiently.
words.example: An integrated transport network, in which buses and trains share a single ticketing system, encourages people to leave their cars at home.

words.definition: A situation in which people have to rely on cars because there are no practical alternatives.
words.example: Poorly planned suburbs have fostered car dependency, as many residents have no realistic alternative to driving.

words.definition: The uncontrolled spread of a city into the surrounding countryside.
words.example: Urban sprawl consumes valuable farmland and lengthens the distances people must travel to work.

words.definition: To close a street or area to vehicles so that only people on foot can use it.
words.example: Pedestrianising city-centre streets can revitalise local businesses and improve air quality.

words.definition: The harmful gases that come out of a vehicle's engine.
words.example: Children living near busy roads are exposed to high levels of exhaust fumes, which can impair lung development.

words.definition: To pay part of the cost of something so that it becomes cheaper for the people who use it.
words.example: Heavily subsidised rail fares would make public transport a more attractive option for commuters.

words.definition: A railway system designed for trains that travel much faster than ordinary trains.
words.example: High-speed rail could significantly reduce journey times between regional cities and the capital.

words.definition: Describing flights or transport that cover relatively short distances.
words.example: Some European countries have restricted short-haul flights on routes where a train journey of under three hours is available.

words.definition: A death caused by an accident, violence or disease.
words.example: Lower speed limits in residential areas have led to a marked reduction in road fatalities.

words.definition: A situation in which traffic is so heavy that vehicles cannot move at all.
words.example: Without investment in public transport, the city's roads will be reduced to gridlock during the rush hour.

words.definition: A part of a road or path that is reserved for bicycles.
words.example: Building segregated cycle lanes makes cycling safer and more appealing to cautious riders.

words.definition: Producing no harmful gases from the exhaust while being used.
words.example: Several cities plan to allow only zero-emission vehicles in their centres within the next decade.

words.definition: An arrangement in which people share the use of cars, or travel together in one car, instead of each owning or driving their own.
words.example: Car-sharing schemes allow urban residents to use a vehicle when they need one without the expense of ownership.
